$comment: Owner: physics-ml. 2.5.0 adds optional splits.overlap_check/manifest/test_groups_disjoint, a structured weights object (a string stays valid), domain_shift, environment and output_semantics. Rules that would change an older artifact's outcome (blank grouping key, empty model_hash, labels or features, training_domain keys and ranges, calibration shape and sample) are semantic checks in contracts/validate.py (_ml_semantics), native from 2.5.0 and applied to older artifacts with --strict.

task.$comment: 2.8.0 adds reweighting (OmniFold, DCTR); each task other than classification needs its validation block (regression_validation, generative_validation, sbi_validation, extrapolation_policy, reweighting_validation)

overlap_check.$comment: 2.5.0: result of a split-overlap / group-leakage check (for example check_split_integrity.py)

manifest.$comment: 2.5.0: path or ref of the split manifest (IDs and groups per split)

test_groups_disjoint.$comment: 2.5.0: no group of the test split appears in training or validation

weights.$comment: 2.5.0: a free-text string (legacy) or a structured declaration

calibration.$comment: shape {method, fit_sample, validation: {metric, sample, before?, after}} is checked semantically (2.5.0); 2.8.0: sample_check {disjoint, fit_sha256, eval_sha256, id_check} as assets/calibration.py records it; disjoint false, equal hashes or names equal after normalization are ml.calibration_on_fit_sample

downstream_validation.$comment: 2.8.0: items {metric (vocab ml_downstream_metrics), quantity_affected, value, uncertainty?, criterion, passed, ref}; free-text items are errors from 2.8.0 (warnings for older artifacts under --strict); every item an ML metric or a bare pass is ml.downstream_ml_only; passed must agree with a numeric value and criterion ('>= 0.68', 'abs < 0.001', 'in [0.9, 1.1]')

domain_shift.$comment: 2.5.0: check of the model on data or control samples (simulation-trained models)

status.$comment: whether the check ran; what it found is outcome (2.8.0)

outcome.$comment: 2.8.0: what was done about the shift; bounded-by-nuisance and uncorrected need nuisance

nuisance.$comment: 2.8.0: the nuisance parameter (name or {name, ref}) that carries the shift in the downstream likelihood

environment.$comment: 2.5.0: software, device, numerical precision and seeds of the training run

parameters.$comment: 2.8.0: model parameters (for example theta of simulation-based inference); training_domain may be declared on them

supervision.$comment: 2.8.0: unsupervised allows empty labels and needs anomaly_validation

regression_validation.$comment: 2.8.0, task regression: response_vs_truth and response_vs_reco (response and resolution in bins of the true and of the reconstructed variable), closure_alt_spectrum (closure on a sample with another truth spectrum), outlier_fraction

generative_validation.$comment: 2.8.0, task generation: observables (physics metrics per observable), two_sample_test {method, power, injected_distortion}, conditioning_range (equal to the training domain)

sbi_validation.$comment: 2.8.0, task inference: coverage, sbc or tarp, and handoff (hep-statistics)

extrapolation_policy.$comment: 2.8.0, task surrogate: action flag|reject|bounded, consumer of the flags

source_files.$comment: 2.8.0: tool outputs the artifact was written from (run summary, split report, calibration, domain-shift and downstream records); files, not contract artifacts, so they are not inputs[]

output_semantics.$comment: 2.5.0: what the model output means; probability and density-ratio need a calibration
